source: Numerics/Sampling/MCMC/Base/MCMCSampler.cs (the delegate constructor) + Numerics/Sampling/MCMC/Gibbs.cs; Numerics/Sampling/Bootstrap/Bootstrap.cs (the four delegate properties); Numerics/Mathematics/Integration/{MonteCarloIntegration.cs, Miser.cs, Vegas.cs, Integrands.cs} @ 2a0357a
reference: Numerics @ 2a0357a. Two cases, each nesting two sub-blocks shaped exactly like a "callback"-kind case's construct/assertions: an "mcmc" block (group "mcmc", method "sample") and a "bootstrap" block (group "bootstrap", method "run"). The nesting is the point. Every other callback fixture pins ACCURACY against the real C# library at that file's relative tolerance; this file's job is the CROSS-LANGUAGE guarantee on the CALLBACK path, so EVERY assertion below is spelled mode "abs" with tol 0, i.e. bit equality in all four runners, not a tolerance. It is the callback layer's counterpart to fixtures/toolbox/toolbox_cross_language.json and fixtures/estimation/fit_cross_language.json. WHAT THE PACKAGES PROMISE AND WHERE IT STOPS: on the registry path every operation happens inside the shared C++ core, so a seeded run is bit-identical between R and Python by construction. On the callback path the draws still come from the core generator, but the log-density (or the proposal, or the statistic) is arithmetic the HOST language evaluates, and R and Python do not guarantee identical rounding for the same formula. MCMC amplifies that without mercy: one flipped accept-or-reject changes every state after it, so chains diverge outright rather than drift. Both callbacks used here are therefore built from + - * / and comparisons alone, with every summation written as an explicit loop rather than any language's sum()/mean()/Average() (R accumulates those in extended precision where C++, Python and C# accumulate in double). Arithmetic-only callbacks are IEEE-deterministic, so they reproduce exactly; a callback that calls log() or exp() need not, and the two worked examples (site/examples/14-custom-posterior, 15-custom-bootstrap) say so in prose rather than leaving it implied. WHY THESE TWO CONSTRUCTS AND NOT WIDER ONES: the constructs were chosen by measurement, not by taste. R and Python agree bit for bit on EVERY callback case in this directory, including the DEMCz two-parameter regression posterior of fixtures/callback/mcmc.json. They agree with the real C# library only where the arithmetic that produces the number lives in the CALLBACK rather than in the compiled core, because clang and gcc contract `a*b + c` into a fused multiply-add by default and .NET does not: on the DEMCz case that gap is 1.5e-14 on the posterior mean and 7e-15 on a late chain state, well inside every other fixture's rel 1e-12 but not zero. The Gibbs case has no such gap. Its recorded states are exact full-conditional draws, `lo + u * (hi - lo)` evaluated in the host language off the core generator, and its posterior mean, median and MAP are a plain sum, an order statistic and a maximum over those states, none of which the core can fuse. So this file pins the quantities that are bit-identical in all four runners and says here, in the open, which ones are not: posterior_sd and ess accumulate `d*d` inside the core and reproduce C#-vs-package to 1.4e-16 and 4.6e-14 rather than exactly, so they are deliberately absent below rather than pinned at a loosened tolerance. THE MCMC BLOCK IS THE GIBBS SAMPLER on purpose: it is the one sampler neither package could reach before this phase, because Gibbs requires a proposal delegate and the packages had no way to pass one. THE SECOND CASE, linear_model_contractible_arithmetic_short_exact, EXISTS TO MAKE ONE COMPILER FLAG DEMONSTRABLE. core/CMakeLists.txt compiles the C++ catalog (core/tests/fixture_callback_catalog.cpp) with -ffp-contract=off, because clang and gcc otherwise fuse `a*b + c` into a single multiply-add and the C++ counterpart of a callback then computes a different function from the R, Python and C# ones. The first case cannot detect that: the callbacks it names are comparisons (Mcmc_UniformWidthKernel) and index draws (Resample_Iid), neither of which has a product to fuse, and removing the flag left the entire fixture tree green. This case names arithmetic the compiler does fuse and pins it at tol 0, so removing the flag fails here. Both of its blocks work on the same straight line through the same eight observations: the mcmc block samples y = a + b*t under Mcmc_LinearKernel, the bootstrap block resamples those y and fits them with Fit_LinearTrend. Two assertions carry the demonstration, both measured by building the catalog each way (Apple clang 21, arm64). statistic[0], the intercept of the ORIGINAL fit, moves by about 50 ulp (0.03571428571428292 written against 0.035714285714283256 fused), because `ybar - slope * tbar` subtracts two nearly equal quantities and so amplifies a last-bit difference in the slope; map_fitness moves by 1 ulp, which is the whole size of the effect on a single kernel evaluation. THE MCMC SEED IS A MEASURED CHOICE rather than a decoration: 72% of the kernel's values over this proposal box differ between the fused and unfused forms, but map_fitness is the maximum over one particular chain, and at seed 12345 -- the seed the first case uses -- the state that wins it falls in the other 28%. Seed 22 is the nearest one where it does not. Nothing else in the mcmc block can move: Gibbs accepts unconditionally and Prop_UniformBox ignores the state it is handed, so the chain is a sequence of independent draws and the log-density's only mark on the run is the fitness recorded beside each state. WHAT THIS CASE DOES NOT PROVE: on x86-64 no compiler may emit a fused multiply-add unless FMA is enabled (-mfma, or -march=x86-64-v3 and up), so on a default Linux or Windows x86-64 build the flag is inert and removing it changes nothing here. The demonstration is real on arm64 and on any x86-64 build with FMA turned on. AN HONEST ODDITY IN ITS BOOTSTRAP BLOCK: statistic[0] is 0.036 while the resampled interval for that same quantity runs from 2.86 to 15.23. That is correct rather than broken -- an iid resample destroys the order the trend lives in, so a replicate's slope is near zero and its intercept near the sample mean, 9.0. The block pins arithmetic; it is not estimating a trend. EVERY expected value is EMITTER-READ from the real Numerics classes driven by tools/oracle_emitter, never a value computed by this repo's own C++. THE THIRD CASE nests a single sub-block, "pivotal", rather than the mcmc/bootstrap pair the first two carry: the sub-blocks are read off the case by name in all four runners, so a case may nest one or five. Its job is the pivotal bootstrap's own cross-language guarantee -- the covariance-aware fit, both Cholesky factorizations, the reflection between them and the diagnostics counts -- proved bit-identical in R, Python, C++ and C#. It can be asserted at zero tolerance because the callback is arithmetic plus one sqrt, IEEE 754's one correctly-rounded transcendental-looking function; a callback using log or exp could not be. THE FOURTH CASE, quadrature_nd_short_exact (P2 "math extras", Task 6), nests one sub-block per stochastic integrator class -- "monte_carlo", "miser", "vegas" -- proving what IS a cross-language guarantee for the Task-5 port, and being explicit about what is not. MonteCarloIntegration's ONLY source of randomness is the seeded `random` member (UseSobolSequence is a documented dead property upstream, so a seeded run reproduces bit for bit without touching the direction-numbers file at all); Miser and Vegas draw from a Sobol low-discrepancy sequence by default, deterministic over the identical new-joe-kuo-6 file every runner ships, so THEIR two blocks reproduce without a seed at all -- the miser block passes one anyway (999) to prove it is inert under use_sobol=true, and the vegas block omits it entirely to prove the same the other way. All three callbacks (Nd_PI, Nd_GSL, NdW_SumOfNormals3) are arithmetic/comparisons plus the already-oracle-validated Normal.StandardZ (never reimplemented -- see fixtures/callback/math.json's own reference note). ONLY function_evaluations and status are asserted here, and that is a measured choice, not an oversight: unlike the mcmc/bootstrap/pivotal cases above, whose CALLBACKS are the only place contractible arithmetic lives, MonteCarloIntegration/Miser/Vegas THEMSELVES (numerics/math/integration/{monte_carlo_integration,miser,vegas}.hpp) are core code, and core/CMakeLists.txt's -ffp-contract=off is deliberately scoped to the fixture_callback_catalog.cpp translation unit alone, NEVER the shared core -- extending it would make this C++ runner exercise a DIFFERENTLY-compiled core than the one R and Python actually ship (see that file's own comment). That means R, Python and this C++ runner all compile MonteCarloIntegration/Miser/Vegas with the SAME (fused) semantics as each other, but not necessarily the SAME as .NET's never-fused one, on formulas with a near-cancelling subtraction -- `avg2 - avg*avg` for MonteCarloIntegration's own standard error, the analogous term inside Miser, and `sum_chi_squared_ - sum_weighted_results_ * result_` for Vegas's chi-squared. Measured directly (isolated single-file recompiles of each header, Apple clang 21 arm64): the fused (shipped) build reproduces the C#-emitted result exactly for two of the three classes and misses by 1 ULP on the third, reproduces standard_error to the bit for one class and misses by 1-3 ULP for the other two, and misses Vegas's chi_squared by ~1.1e-7 relative -- while recompiling with -ffp-contract=off (which nothing ships with) reproduces every one of those fields to the bit. Since the shipped build is the one this fixture must describe, and since which floating-point field happens to land on a matching ULP is a property of the exact seed/settings chosen rather than a guarantee, only function_evaluations and status -- both integers/enums with no floating-point path -- are pinned at zero tolerance; fixtures/callback/math.json's own three EMITTER-READ cases pin the floating-point fields at a measured, non-zero relative tolerance instead. NO oracle_skip and NO loosened tolerance is applied to the fields left unasserted here; they are simply not asserted, the same practice this repository's other chaotic/FMA-sensitive fixtures follow.

callbacks.Mcmc_UniformWidthKernel: f(mu) = 0 when every |x - mu| <= 1 over x = {4.9, 5.1, 5.0, 5.2, 4.8}, else -infinity  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/mcmc.json documents: the log-likelihood of x_i ~ Uniform(mu - 1, mu + 1) with the normalizing term dropped. Comparisons only, so it cannot round differently anywhere]
callbacks.Prop_UniformConditional: proposal(parameters, prng) = lo + prng.NextDouble() * (hi - lo), lo = max(x) - 1 = 4.2, hi = min(x) + 1 = 5.8  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/mcmc.json documents, upstream's Gibbs.Proposal(double[], Random) shape: the EXACT full conditional of Mcmc_UniformWidthKernel under a flat prior, so every recorded state is an independent Uniform(4.2, 5.8) draw. One NextDouble per call, off the generator the sampler hands in]
callbacks.Resample_Iid: resample(data, parameters, prng) -> n draws of data[prng.Next(0, n)], n = data.Length  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/bootstrap.json documents: the ordinary nonparametric resample, every index drawn off the generator the replicate hands in]
callbacks.Fit_Mean: fit(data) -> [sum(data) / data.Length], summed in an explicit loop  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/bootstrap.json documents]
callbacks.Stat_Identity: statistic(parameters) -> parameters  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/bootstrap.json documents: the statistic IS the fitted parameter, so the interval is an interval on the mean]
callbacks.Mcmc_LinearKernel: f(a, b) = -0.5 * sum((y_i - a - b*t_i)^2) over t = 1..8 and y = {2.1, 3.9, 6.2, 7.8, 10.1, 12.2, 13.8, 16.1}, accumulated in an explicit loop  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/mcmc.json documents. The second case's kernel, and the CONTRACTIBLE one: `y - a - b*t` and `acc + r*r` are both the shape a C++ compiler fuses into a multiply-add]
callbacks.Prop_UniformBox: proposal(parameters, prng) = [lo_j + prng.NextDouble() * (hi_j - lo_j)] for lo = (-1, 1.5), hi = (1, 2.5)  [the two-parameter member of the proposal catalog. An INDEPENDENCE proposal: it ignores the state it is handed, so with Gibbs accepting unconditionally the chain is a sequence of independent draws from that box. The box brackets the least-squares fit of Mcmc_LinearKernel's eight observations (intercept ~0.036, slope ~1.998) and sits strictly inside the priors]
callbacks.Fit_LinearTrend: fit(data) -> [ybar - slope * tbar, slope], slope = sum(dt*dy) / sum(dt*dt) over t = 1..n, in an explicit loop  [the contraction-bearing member of the bootstrap catalog: every accumulation is `acc + a*b` and the intercept then subtracts two nearly equal quantities, so the fused and unfused values differ well past the last bit. sum(dt*dt) depends only on n, so no resample can make the fit fail]
callbacks.FitCov_NormalMLE: fit_with_covariance(data) -> (parameters = [mean, population sd], covariance = diag(s2/n, s2/(2n))), summed in explicit loops  [corehydro addition, upstream's Func<TData, BootstrapFit> shape: the delegate the PIVOTAL run type fits through. Arithmetic plus one sqrt -- and sqrt is the one libm function IEEE 754 requires to be correctly rounded, so unlike log or exp it is the same value in R, Python, C++ and C#, which is what lets this case be asserted at zero tolerance at all]
callbacks.Nd_PI: f(x) = (x[0]^2 + x[1]^2 < 1) ? 1 : 0  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/math.json documents (P2 "math extras", Task 6): comparisons and one multiply-add per dimension, so it cannot round differently anywhere]
callbacks.Nd_GSL: f(x) = (1 / pi^3) / (1 - cos(x[0]) cos(x[1]) cos(x[2]))  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/math.json documents]
callbacks.NdW_SumOfNormals3: f(x, weight) = sum_i mu20[i] + sigma20[i] * Normal.StandardZ(x[i]) for i in 0..2, weight ignored  [the same catalog callback fixtures/callback/math.json documents; StandardZ is the already-ported, oracle-validated inverse standard Normal CDF, reused rather than reimplemented -- see that file's reference note]
